refnamediv.refpurpose: Sign system reports with a verified timestamp from a Timestamp Authority (TSA).

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: systemd-report-sign-tsa@.service is a system service that signs system reports generated by systemd-report1. It is a signing backend for the --sign= logic of that tool: it implements the io.systemd.Report.Signer.Sign() Varlink method and is reached via a socket linked into the /run/systemd/report.sign/ directory, named tsa.

The service is socket-activated (one instance per connection) via systemd-report-sign-tsa.socket. Rather than signing with a local key, it obtains an RFC 3161 timestamp token from a remote Time Stamping Authority. The digest passed to it is embedded in the message imprint of a TimeStampReq, which is then submitted to the TSA over HTTP, cryptographically binding the TSA's attestation of time to the system report being signed.

The returned signature carries the DER binary timestamp token structure containing the TSA's signature on the messsage imprint, the timestamp in human readable format and the URL of the TSA that produced it.

Responses are checked before being accepted; the status must indicate the timestamp was granted, the nonce must match the randomly genrated nonce from the request, the message imprint must match the digest that was sent, and the token's signature must verify against a certificate chain rooted in the system trust store. A TS whose certificate does not chain to a trusted root is rejected.

This backend requires network access to the configured TSA and is therefore subject to the availabilty of the external service. On systems where the TSA cannot be reached or declines to issue a timestamp, the signing operation fails and the mechanism is skipped. The service keeps no persistent state.
